parts.latex:
The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic series is given by $S_n=2n(n+2)$.

Find the first term and the common difference of the series.

solutions.latex:
$S_n=2n(n+2)$
$$\begin{aligned}\therefore\ T_1&=S_1=6\\ T_2&=S_2-S_1\\ &=16-6\\ &=10\end{aligned}$$
Hence the common difference is $T_2-T_1=4$.
criteria: Substantial progress, e.g. finds the first term

meta.top_criterion_original: Finds value of first two terms and hence the common difference

parts.latex:
The sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic sequence is $S_n=3n^2-4n$, where $n>1$.

Find the $n$th term, $T_n$, \underline{\textbf{and}} state the common difference.

meta.top_criterion_original: Marks not itemised on the copy (3 marks): use of $T_n=S_n-S_{n-1}$; $T_n=6n-7$; $d=6$
meta.rubric_note: Source gives 3 marks without itemising them (use of T_n = S_n - S_(n-1); T_n = 6n - 7; d = 6); written top-down in that order.

solutions.latex:
Write each term as a multiple of $\ln 3$:

$$\begin{aligned} \sum_{n=4}^{n}\ln 3^{2n} &= \ln 3^8+\ln 3^{10}+\ln 3^{12}+\ldots+\ln 3^{2n} \\ &= 8\ln 3+10\ln 3+12\ln 3+\ldots+2n\ln 3 \\ &= \ln 3\,(8+10+12+\ldots+2n) \end{aligned}$$

The bracket is an arithmetic series with $a=8$, $d=2$ and last term $l=2n$.

Running from $4$ to $n$, it has $n-3$ terms, and the sum is $\dfrac{\text{number of terms}}{2}(a+l)$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Sum} &= \ln 3\left[\dfrac{n-3}{2}(8+2n)\right] \\ &= \ln 3\left[\dfrac{n-3}{2}\cdot 2(4+n)\right] \\ &= (n-3)(n+4)\ln 3 \end{aligned}$$

Rationalise the denominator.
$$\begin{aligned} \sum_{r=1}^{63}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r+1}+\sqrt{r}} &= \sum_{r=1}^{63}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r+1}+\sqrt{r}}\times\dfrac{\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}}{\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}}\right) \\ &= \sum_{r=1}^{63}\left(\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}\right) \end{aligned}$$
The terms telescope.
$$\begin{aligned} \sum_{r=1}^{63}\left(\sqrt{r+1}-\sqrt{r}\right) &= (\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1})+(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})+\cdots+(\sqrt{63}-\sqrt{62})+(\sqrt{64}-\sqrt{63}) \\ &= -1+\sqrt{64} \\ &= 7 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Rationalises the denominator, or equivalent merit
